page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX and AVX512F instructions, though it lacks newer AVX-512 VNNI capabilities. The instance is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

A defining characteristic of the ecs.d1.3xlarge is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 35,433 GB of HDD capacity. This high storage density makes it highly cost-efficient for bulk data retention, though the reliance on HDD technology presents a performance tradeoff compared to solid-state alternatives. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 8,789.97 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,584.0. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 911.0 and a poor single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.96 GB/sec. Memory performance is also modest, with a Passmark memory score in the bottom 25%.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.d1.3xlarge is best suited for workloads requiring massive local storage capacity with moderate compute requirements. Appropriate use cases include large-scale data warehousing, log archiving, cold storage repositories, MapReduce deployments, and distributed file systems. It is less suitable for latency-sensitive databases or high-performance single-threaded applications due to its slower single-core execution and HDD-based storage media.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-optimized instance featuring 12 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of RAM. Its primary differentiator is a massive 35,433 GB of local HDD storage, offering high capacity and resource density for bulk data workloads. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers average multi-core CPU performance, as shown by its Geekbench multi-core score of 4,584.0, but exhibits weak single-core performance and modest memory bandwidth. With a baseline network speed of 4 Gbps and no GPU acceleration, this instance is highly cost-efficient for storage-heavy, throughput-oriented tasks. It is best suited for distributed file systems, log processing, data warehousing, and large-scale archiving where massive storage volume is prioritized over low-latency disk I/O.
